observations.print_location: Praefatio p. X (OCR web excerpt line 131)
observations.source_short_quote: Ex uno eodemque archetypo iam mutilo
observations.literal_scope: Boer considers it probable that the described subarchetypes descend from one already-mutilated exemplar (verisimile); expressed as a conjecture, not a proved physical stemma.

observations.print_location: Praefatio p. VII (OCR web excerpt lines 73–74)
observations.literal_scope: All three manuscripts appear explicitly in Boer's inventory; OCR glyphs used for some sigla are unsafe to transcribe.

observations.print_location: Praefatio pp. X–XI (OCR web excerpt lines 136–137)
observations.interpretation: Boer explicitly preferred the Z recension to the others for textual work, citing preservation of readings less corrupted than other witnesses; this is relative editor judgment, not an observed trigon table.
observations.dates_noted_in_previous_research: C15 called Z 13th-century from catalogue; preserve difference as dating discrepancy, not resolved

observations.print_location: Praefatio p. XI (OCR web excerpt lines 136–137)
observations.interpretation: Despite its difficult orthography, Boer calls Y valuable for preserving older glyphs, number forms and recapitulation; not equivalent to proof its monomoiria grid is earliest.

observations.print_location: Praefatio p. IX (OCR web excerpt line 128)
observations.interpretation: One manuscript excerpt of trigon monomoiria is attributed to Paulus rather than Heliodorus within Boer's contents inventory; exact OCR witness siglum is unreadable and needs printed apparatus inspection.

observations.print_location: Praefatio p. X (OCR web excerpt lines 130–136)
observations.interpretation: Boer reports surviving excerpts and scribal accretions, variable chapters and headings, and substantial mutilation; the edited Greek cannot be treated as a unique pristine authorial 4th-century implementation.
